title: How to start selling on Amazon Australia in 2026: the complete beginner's guide
description: Sell on Amazon.com.au in 2026: A$49.95 plan, June 2026 FBA fee cuts, GST and the A$75,000 threshold, ACCC safety rules, and your first 90 days.
tldr: Amazon Australia's sales hit A$4.77 billion in 2025, up from A$3.81 billion, and seller-fee revenue rose to A$1.14 billion [s12][s11].
Choose the Professional plan (A$49.95/month excl. GST); the Individual plan (A$0.99/item) can't advertise [s1].
Referral fees are mostly 6–15% with no minimum; Amazon cut selected FBA fees from 10 June 2026, with lower fees for items under A$13 [s1].
Register for GST once turnover reaches A$75,000; Amazon collects 10% GST on imported items worth A$1,000 or less shipped from overseas [s22][s18][s23].
Overseas sellers who keep stock in Australia can't use simplified GST registration; plan for standard registration with an ABN [s21][s20].
Consignments over A$1,000 need an import declaration, plus processing and biosecurity charges, duty and import GST [s24][s25][s26].
Avoid button batteries, magnets and mains-powered items for a first product: mandatory standards and EESS rules apply, and the ACCC is enforcing them on marketplaces [s28][s29][s37].
Australian Consumer Law guarantees can't be excluded: no 'no refunds' terms [s33][s34].

blocks.p: Amazon.com.au is still a young marketplace compared with Amazon.com or Amazon.co.uk, but it is growing fast. Amazon's Australian filings for calendar 2025 show total sales of **A$4.77 billion**, up from A$3.81 billion in 2024 [s12]. Amazon's own direct product sales on the Australian site reached A$2.33 billion, up 20% year on year [s11].

The part that matters most to you is the money Amazon earns from independent sellers. Revenue from **third-party seller services** (the fees sellers like you pay) reached **A$1.14 billion** in 2025, up from A$839 million [s11][s12]. A third-party seller is any business that lists its own products on Amazon, as opposed to Amazon selling stock it bought itself. Fast growth in that line means more sellers, more orders, or both.

blocks.p: Advertising is Amazon Australia's fastest-growing line. It went from A$242 million in 2024, up 58.1% [s13], to A$392.2 million in 2025 [s11]. More advertisers bidding on the same search results usually means higher cost per click over time. Plan your budget on the assumption that ads will get more expensive, not cheaper.

Globally, third-party sellers sold about **62% of units and 69% of the value** of goods sold on Amazon in 2025, according to Marketplace Pulse [s14]. The same research found that the number of new sellers joining Amazon worldwide in 2025 was the lowest since it began tracking in 2015, down 44% on 2024 [s14]. Fewer newcomers is good news for you: the field is not getting flooded the way it was in 2020–2021.

In the US, Amazon's AI shopping assistant Rufus was folded into a new assistant called **Alexa for Shopping** in May 2026 [s15]. We could not confirm that Rufus or Alexa for Shopping is live for Amazon.com.au shoppers at the time of writing. Either way, the direction is clear: shoppers increasingly ask questions in plain language and get answers built from your listing text, images, reviews and Q&A. Write listings that answer real questions (size, materials, what is in the box, who it is for), not keyword lists.

callout.title: What this means for a beginner
callout.text: Australia is big enough to build a real business, small enough that many niches still have only a handful of serious sellers, and growing at 20%+ a year [s11][s12]. The catch: ad spend is growing even faster [s13][s11], so your margins must survive paid traffic from day one.

blocks.p: We could not confirm whether Amazon runs a separate low-price storefront (like Haul in the US) on Amazon.com.au. Check the Amazon.com.au homepage and Seller Central news before you plan around one. For category data (what is growing or saturated), use Amazon's own Product Opportunity Explorer once your account is open; it shows search volume and growth by niche for this marketplace.
These are the changes a beginner should know about. Fees and rules change often, so treat this as a starting point and check **Seller Central News** weekly.

sections.title: Is Amazon Australia right for you?

ul: **Australian residents and businesses.** You can open an account with local ID, a local bank account and (for a business) an ABN or ACN [s3]. Your stock, customers and tax office are all in one country.
**Sellers with a product that suits Australian life**: outdoor, pet, home, baby and similar everyday categories, where you can ship stock into an Amazon warehouse here.

**Overseas brands that already sell in the US or UK** and want a second, less crowded market. Amazon lets merged accounts list in other stores, with a separate Professional fee of US$39.99 a month split across the countries where you have active listings [s1].
People hoping for US-level volume. Amazon Australia's total sales of A$4.77 billion in 2025 [s12] are a small fraction of Amazon's US business. Niches are smaller, so order fewer units per product.
Anyone planning to ship small parcels from overseas one at a time. It works, but delivery is slow compared with Prime, and Amazon will collect 10% GST on those sales [s23], which you must price in.
Sellers of electrical goods, toys for young children, or products with button batteries who are not ready to handle Australian safety rules (see Compliance) [s29][s36].

blocks.h3: Selling from outside Australia (India, China, US, UK and elsewhere)

blocks.p: Overseas sellers can register. Amazon asks for a government ID, proof of address, a chargeable credit card, a bank account for payouts and tax information [s2][s3]. Amazon accepts Visa, Mastercard or Amex credit or debit cards that can be charged internationally; prepaid cards, gift certificates and services like PayPal are not accepted [s3][s4]. Amazon pays your sales proceeds into a bank account [s1], so you need an account that can receive Australian-dollar payouts in a country Amazon supports. Check the deposit-method list during sign-up.
There are two models for overseas sellers:

ul: **Ship from overseas to each customer.** Goods worth A$1,000 or less are "low value imported goods", and Amazon calculates, collects and pays the 10% GST to the ATO [s23][s18]. Simple, but slow delivery hurts conversion.

**Ship stock into Australia first (FBA or a local warehouse).** Delivery is fast and you can get the Prime badge. But because the goods are already in Australia when sold, the sale is not a low-value import: you have your own GST obligation and the ATO says you cannot use simplified GST registration [s21]. Most overseas sellers in this model use standard GST registration with an ABN, and often an Australian registered tax agent [s20].

callout.title: Don't skip the tax step
callout.text: If you warehouse stock in Australia and your GST turnover reaches A$75,000 a year, you must register for GST [s22]. Get advice before you ship your first container, not after.

blocks.p: If you plan to run ads (and you should), choose **Professional**. You can't advertise on the Individual plan [s1], and at 51 items a month the Individual per-item fee already costs more than the flat A$49.95 (51 × A$0.99 = A$50.49) [s1].

blocks.h3: Identity verification and the video call

blocks.p: Amazon runs **Seller Identity Verification** before your account goes live [s4]. You choose either **Instant Identity Verification** (a photo of your face and your ID) or a **video call** with an Amazon associate [s3][s4]. On the call you show the **original** documents you uploaded at registration, including your ID and your bank or card statement [s4]; copies or different documents are not accepted [s5]. Sellers on the Australian forums report long waits to connect; if a call fails you can book a new one, and if your account stays deactivated after the call, contact Seller Support or Account Health [s5].

Amazon says you can often finish registration in a few hours, and identity verification usually takes **four business days or less** [s3]. Allow longer if a document is rejected or you wait for a video-call slot. Amazon may also ask for extra documents later, depending on where you want to sell [s3].

blocks.h3: Common reasons for delay or rejection

ul: Name or address on the ID doesn't match the name or address typed in the form.
Proof of address is older than allowed [s4] or is a screenshot instead of a full statement.
Using a prepaid card, gift card or PayPal as your payment method [s3].
Bringing different documents (or copies) to the video call [s5].
Opening a second account without meeting Amazon's conditions [s3], or being linked to a previously suspended account (shared card, bank, address or device).

ol: Decide: sole trader or company. Get an ABN (Australian residents) or decide on your GST registration route (overseas).

Open the payout bank account in the exact legal name you will register with.
Use one device and one internet connection you will keep using.
Keep the originals beside you for the video call [s5].

blocks.p: All Amazon fees below are quoted excluding GST unless stated. Fees change; always confirm in Seller Central or with Amazon's Revenue Calculator before you order stock.

blocks.h3: Referral fees (Amazon's commission on each sale)

blocks.p: A **referral fee** is a percentage of the total sale price that Amazon keeps. Most are between 6% and 15% depending on category. It is calculated on the total sales price, including delivery and gift wrapping, and Amazon Australia has no minimum or maximum referral fee [s1]. Some categories use a split rate based on price.

blocks.p: This section is general information, not tax advice. Rules are set by the **Australian Taxation Office (ATO)**; use their pages or an Australian registered tax agent for your situation.

**GST (Goods and Services Tax)** is Australia's 10% consumption tax. You must register for GST when your current or projected GST turnover reaches **A$75,000** a year (A$150,000 for non-profits) [s22][s40]. Below that, registration is optional. Once registered, you charge GST on Australian sales, lodge activity statements, and can usually claim back GST you paid on business costs, including GST paid at the border on imports [s20][s27].

blocks.h3: Low-value imported goods: when Amazon collects GST

blocks.p: Goods with a customs value of **A$1,000 or less** (except tobacco and alcohol) that are shipped from overseas to Australian consumers are "low value imported goods" [s18]. When these are sold through an **electronic distribution platform** like Amazon, the platform operator is generally treated as the supplier and is responsible for the GST [s18]. Amazon confirms it calculates, collects and remits 10% GST on low value imported goods sold by third-party sellers and shipped from overseas, applied per item even if the order total is above A$1,000 [s23]. Those sales don't count towards your own GST turnover [s18].

callout.title: FBA stock is not a low-value import
callout.text: Once your goods are in an Australian warehouse, the sale happens in Australia. The ATO says a non-resident who imports goods, warehouses them here and then sells online has its own GST obligation for those sales and cannot use simplified registration [s21].

ul: Get an **ABN** (free via the Australian Business Register). Amazon accepts an ABN or ACN as your business registration number [s3], and the Amazon Business program asks for an ABN or a Statement by a Supplier form [s39].

Amazon can't produce a GST tax invoice for third-party sellers who are not registered for GST [s23], which may matter to business buyers.

blocks.p: When you ship stock into Australia (for example, from China or India to an FBA warehouse), you are the importer:

ul: Consignments over **A$1,000** need a full **Import Declaration**, and all duties, taxes and charges must be paid before the goods are released [s24].
**Import processing charge** examples: A$90 for a documentary declaration on A$1,000–A$10,000 consignments; A$152 electronic and A$192 documentary at A$10,000 or more [s25].
A separate **biosecurity charge** applies to full import declarations: A$48 by air, A$71 by sea [s26].
**Customs duty** depends on your product's tariff classification; there is no single rate [s24].
**Import GST** is 10% of the value of the taxable importation, which includes customs value, duty, and transport and insurance to Australia [s27].
Most beginners use a licensed customs broker or a freight forwarder who handles the declaration.

blocks.p: Profit from selling is taxable income. Australian residents report it through their sole trader or company tax return. Overseas sellers are generally taxed at home but should check their country's tax treaty with Australia. Keep every invoice, freight bill and Amazon settlement report.

ul: Before your first import if you are overseas and plan to use FBA.
When you approach A$75,000 in turnover [s22].
When you choose between sole trader and company.
If you sell in more than one country.

blocks.p: Australia enforces product safety hard, and online marketplaces are a stated ACCC priority [s31]. The **ACCC (Australian Competition and Consumer Commission)** runs product safety through productsafety.gov.au. Its view is that safety rules apply to marketplaces that possess or control goods, just as they apply to other suppliers [s28]. As the seller, you are responsible for your product being legal.

Some categories and products need Amazon's approval before you can list them ("gated"), and some are banned. The list changes; check **Add a Product** in Seller Central, which tells you if approval is needed. Beginners should avoid gated categories for a first product.

Australia has **four mandatory standards** for button and coin batteries and products that contain them: two safety standards (batteries must be secured so children can't easily remove them, plus testing) and two information standards (warnings on packaging and instructions) [s29][s30]. Online listings must also show a visible, prominent, legible warning [s30]. The ACCC's first Federal Court case against an online marketplace over mandatory standards concerned children's backpacks allegedly sold without these warnings [s28].

callout.title: High-risk products for beginners
callout.text: Anything with a button battery, small powerful magnets [s32], children's toys, or mains-powered electrical items. Each has extra rules, testing and enforcement attention.

blocks.p: There are many more mandatory safety and information standards (for example toys for young children, cots, and other children's products). Before you order, search the ACCC's **Search mandatory standards** tool on productsafety.gov.au for your product type, and ask your supplier for test reports to the Australian standard, not just a CE or US certificate.

Mains-powered electrical goods fall under the **Electrical Equipment Safety System (EESS)** [s36]. Equipment is rated Level 1, 2 or 3 by risk. Level 2 and Level 3 equipment must be registered on the national database, and Level 3 equipment also needs a certificate of conformity [s37]. The **responsible supplier** is whoever makes or imports the goods into Australia, and must also be registered [s37]. Compliant products carry the **RCM (Regulatory Compliance Mark)** [s38]. If you're an overseas seller, you usually need an Australian entity or partner to act as responsible supplier.

blocks.h3: Australian Consumer Law: refunds and warranties

ul: **Consumer guarantees apply automatically** and can't be removed by your terms [s33][s34].
**Major failure:** the customer chooses a refund or a replacement [s33].
**Minor failure:** you can choose to repair, replace or refund [s33].
Any warranty you offer is **in addition** to these rights, not instead of them [s35].
You don't have to refund a change of mind under the guarantees [s33] (Amazon's own return policy may still require it).
Don't write "no refunds" or "manufacturer warranty only" in listings or inserts. The ACCC has flagged such terms as potentially misleading [s34].

blocks.p: Use English on packaging, instructions and warnings, and include any warnings a mandatory standard requires [s29]. Make sure product claims ("organic", "waterproof", "BPA-free") are true and you can prove them.

**Amazon Brand Registry** gives brand owners tools to protect their listings and unlocks features such as A+ Content (rich images and text on the product page), Sponsored Brands ads and a Brand Store. It needs a pending or registered trademark [s3]. You can file an Australian trademark with **IP Australia**. We could not verify IP Australia's current processing times or Amazon's list of accepted trademark offices and programs (such as IP Accelerator) for Australia, so check both before planning your launch. File early: the trademark is usually the slowest step.

sections.title: Choosing your first product with data

ul: **Small and light.** The smallest FBA tier costs A$3.20–A$4.55 per unit [s1]; bulky items cost far more to ship and store, especially from October to December [s1].
**Selling price around A$25–A$60.** High enough that a 29% fee share (see the Costs example) still leaves room for product cost and ads.
**Not gated, no batteries, no mains power, not for young children** for your first launch [s29][s32][s37].
**Year-round demand**, not just Christmas or summer.
**Room to be better**: competitors with ratings under about 4.3 stars and reviews that repeat the same complaint you can fix.

blocks.h3: Rule of thumb: the one-third split

blocks.p: A simple target: Amazon fees about one-third of the price, landed product cost about one-third, and the last third for ads, returns and profit. **Example only:** a A$25 baby product with A$7.30 in referral + FBA fees [s1] leaves A$17.70. If landed cost is A$6, you have A$11.70 before storage, ads and returns. Spend A$4 per sale on ads and you keep about A$7.70 a unit, before GST if you are registered.

callout.title: Never buy reviews
callout.text: Paying for reviews, giving free products for reviews, or asking friends and family to review gets accounts suspended. Use Vine and Amazon's Request a Review button only.

ul: **CPC (cost per click)**: what you pay each time someone clicks your ad.
**ACoS (advertising cost of sale)**: ad spend ÷ ad sales. A$20 spent for A$80 of ad sales = 25% ACoS.
**TACoS (total ACoS)**: ad spend ÷ all sales (ads + organic). This shows if ads are lifting your whole business.
**Break-even ACoS**: your profit margin before ads. In the Costs example (A$11.70 margin on A$25), break-even ACoS is about 47%.
**Sponsored Products**: ads for a single product in search results and on product pages. Start here.
**Sponsored Brands**: a banner with your logo and several products. Needs Brand Registry.
**Sponsored Display**: reach shoppers on and off Amazon who viewed similar products. Leave until later.

blocks.p: Ads require the Professional plan [s1]. Amazon's Australian ad business grew 58.1% in 2024 [s13] and reached A$392.2 million in 2025 [s11], so expect competition for clicks to keep rising.

ol: **Auto campaign**: Amazon picks searches. Example budget A$10/day.
**Manual exact campaign**: 10–20 keywords you're confident in. Example budget A$10/day.
After 2 weeks, move search terms that sell from the auto campaign into the exact campaign, and add them as negatives in the auto campaign.

blocks.p: In the first 30 days, an ACoS above break-even is normal while you collect data and reviews. By day 60–90, aim for ACoS below break-even and a TACoS that falls month by month. Your category's CPCs determine the rest; the Amazon Ads console shows suggested bids for each keyword.

A **negative keyword** stops your ad showing for a search. Add searches that get clicks but no sales after a reasonable number of clicks, and searches that are clearly irrelevant (wrong size, wrong product, competitor brand names you can't beat).

ol: Download the search term report.
Add negatives for wasted spend.
Move winners to exact match.
Adjust bids: lower on high-ACoS keywords, raise on profitable ones (small steps).
Check TACoS and stock cover before raising budgets.

ul: **Amazon Vine**: Amazon invites trusted reviewers to get your product free and post honest reviews. Available to Brand Registry sellers; check enrolment fees and limits in Seller Central.
**Request a Review** button: on each order in Seller Central, sends Amazon's standard review request.
A good product, honest listing and helpful insert (no review asks tied to rewards) do the rest.

blocks.p: With Brand Registry you can build a free multi-page **Brand Store** on Amazon and add **A+ Content** to listings. Both help conversion and give you a page to send outside traffic to.

blocks.p: Once you're profitable in Australia, the common next steps are **Amazon.com (US)**, **Amazon.co.uk (UK)**, **Amazon.co.jp (Japan)** and **Amazon.sg (Singapore)**. Merged accounts can list in other Amazon stores, with a separate Professional fee equivalent to US$39.99 a month split across the countries where you have active listings [s1]. Each new country has its own tax registration, product safety rules and fee table, and Amazon may ask for extra documents per country [s3]. Start with one, and treat it like a new launch.
Send your own traffic (social media, email, creators) to your Brand Store or listings. Use Amazon's attribution links in the Ads console, where available, to measure what that traffic does.

ol: **Ignoring Australian safety standards.** Button batteries, magnets and electrical goods have mandatory rules and active enforcement [s28][s29][s32][s37].
**Writing "no refunds" or "warranty only".** Consumer guarantees can't be removed [s33][s34].
**Using simplified GST registration while holding stock in Australia.** The ATO says that's not available to you [s21].

**Buying or incentivising reviews.** Leads to suspension.
**Using brand names or images you don't own.** Leads to IP complaints and listing removals; repeat complaints can suspend your account.
**Unprovable claims** ("medical grade", "organic", "100% safe").
**Letting FBM orders ship late** or without tracking. Late shipment rates hurt your account health.
**No trademark before launch.** No Brand Registry means no A+ Content, Vine or brand protection.
**Ignoring import costs.** Duty, import GST, processing and biosecurity charges add up [s25][s26][s27].
**Running out of stock in your first 90 days.** Rankings drop and you pay to rebuild them.

faq.q: How much does it actually cost to sell on Amazon Australia?
faq.a: The Professional plan is A$49.95 a month excluding GST, or the Individual plan charges A$0.99 per item sold. On top of that you pay a referral fee, mostly 6–15% of the price, and FBA fees if Amazon ships for you. For a small A$25 item, referral plus FBA can be around A$7.

faq.q: Do I need an ABN to sell on Amazon Australia?
faq.a: Not always. Amazon accepts an ABN or ACN for business registrations, and Amazon Business asks for an ABN or a Statement by a Supplier form. Overseas sellers who keep stock in Australia usually need standard GST registration, which uses an ABN.

faq.q: Do I have to register for GST?
faq.a: Only once your GST turnover reaches or is expected to reach A$75,000 a year. Many sellers register earlier so they can claim GST paid on imports and costs. Ask a tax agent for your situation.

faq.q: I'm in India/China. Can I sell on Amazon.com.au?
faq.a: Yes. You need ID, proof of address, an internationally chargeable credit or debit card and a bank account that can receive payouts. If you ship each order from overseas, Amazon collects GST on items up to A$1,000. If you use FBA, you have your own GST obligations and can't use simplified registration.

faq.q: Who collects GST on my Amazon sales?
faq.a: For low value imported goods (A$1,000 or less) shipped from overseas, Amazon collects and pays the 10% GST. For stock already in Australia, it's your responsibility if you're registered or required to register.

faq.q: Is FBA worth it in Australia?
faq.a: For most beginners, yes. FBA gives you the Prime badge and fast delivery, and Amazon cut selected FBA fees from 10 June 2026. Avoid it for bulky, slow-selling items where storage fees eat your margin.

faq.q: How long does Amazon Australia seller verification take?
faq.a: Amazon says registration often takes a few hours and identity verification usually four business days or less. Delays usually come from mismatched documents or waiting for a video-call slot. Bring the original documents you uploaded.
Professional if you'll sell more than about 50 items a month or want to advertise. The Individual plan can't run ads, promotions or bulk listings.

faq.q: Do I need RCM or other certification?
faq.a: If you sell mains-powered electrical goods, they fall under the EESS and may need registration and certification, with an Australian responsible supplier. Products with button batteries have four mandatory standards. Check the ACCC's mandatory standards search for anything aimed at children.

faq.q: Can I put 'no refunds' on my listing?
faq.a: No. Australian Consumer Law guarantees apply automatically. For a major failure the customer chooses a refund or replacement, and warranties can't replace those rights.

faq.q: When is Prime Day in Australia?
faq.a: In 2026 it ran for seven days, 7–13 July, on different dates from the US. Watch Seller Central for 2027 dates and deal deadlines.

faq.q: How much should I spend on ads at the start?
faq.a: There's no official number. A common approach is a small daily budget split across one auto and one exact Sponsored Products campaign, then cutting waste weekly. Make sure your margin can survive the ad cost.

faq.q: Is Amazon Australia too competitive now?
faq.a: It's growing fast: total sales went from A$3.81 billion in 2024 to A$4.77 billion in 2025. Many niches still have few serious sellers, but ad costs are rising, so pick products with healthy margins.
